q: A Botnet is

options.A: A group of internet connected devices affected and controlled by a malware
options.B: A group of connected agencies with malicious intents
options.C: It is used for stealing data, sending spam and DDoS attack

e: Both A & C — that is the right answer. The correct option is (D) Both A & C: a botnet is a group of internet-connected devices infected and controlled by malware, and it is used for stealing data, sending spam and launching DDoS attacks. The devices ('bots') obey a command-and-control server without their owners' knowledge. Exam note: DDoS (Distributed Denial of Service) floods a target with traffic to make it unavailable. Notice how precisely the correct option is worded.

q: Unsolicited commercial email is known as
e: Spam — that is the right answer. The correct option is (A) Spam: unsolicited commercial email — bulk messages sent without the recipient's consent — is called spam. Spam filters and anti-spam laws exist to control it. Exam note: spam is distinct from malware; spam is unwanted content, while malware is software designed to harm. The principle behind this is worth grasping, not just memorising: once you understand why the rule is framed this way, the answer follows naturally instead of needing rote recall.

q: Hiding original data with modified content to protect sensitive personal or commercial data is
e: The correct answer is Data Masking. The correct option is (C) Data Masking: replacing original sensitive data with modified or fictional content to protect it is called data masking. It is used in testing and analytics so that real personal or commercial data is never exposed. Exam note: masking differs from encryption — masked data is not meant to be reversed, while encrypted data can be decrypted with the key.
